steps.ask: The diagonal PR splits the parallelogram. What is the area of triangle PQR?
steps.title: Area of triangle $PQR$

lines.text: The diagonal $[PR]$ cuts the parallelogram into two triangles of equal area.

steps.ask: M is the midpoint of QR. How does triangle PQM compare with triangle PQR, and what is its area?
steps.title: Area of triangle $PQM$

lines.text: $M$ is the midpoint of $[QR]$. Triangles $PQM$ and $PQR$ have the same height from $P$, so $PQM$ has half the area.

problems.note: The whole parallelogram is 480 m² and E is the midpoint of [CD] rather than M on [QR], and the answer asks for two areas. The same two steps are used: the diagonal halves the area, then a midpoint halves a triangle.

legend.1: the answer, the area of triangle BCE

steps.ask: The diagonal BD cuts the parallelogram in two. What is the area of triangle ABD?
steps.title: Find the area of triangle ABD

lines.text: The diagonal $[BD]$ cuts the parallelogram into two triangles of equal area.

steps.ask: E is the midpoint of CD. How does triangle BCE compare with triangle BCD, and what is its area?
steps.title: Find the area of triangle BCE

lines.text: Triangle $BCD$ is the other half of the parallelogram, so its area is $\hl{2}{240\text{ m}^2}$.
$E$ is the midpoint of $[CD]$, so $[CE]$ is half of $[CD]$. Triangles $BCE$ and $BCD$ have the same height from $B$, so $BCE$ has half the area.

problems.note: The areas are now algebraic expressions, so the answer is x found from an equation rather than an area. The diagonal still gives equal areas, so the method is the same.
